findings: Corrected the conjecture statement to c <= K_epsilon rad(abc)^(1+epsilon), with pairwise coprimality and the epsilon-dependent constant explicit.
Removed the inaccurate claim that IUT simply separates addition and multiplication into different universes; the short description now follows the author’s overview and PRIMS abstract.

Replaced the false Fermat inequality derivation. The conditional implication uses the infinitely many power triples from any hypothetical primitive Fermat solution, whose radical is fixed while c grows.
Distinguished Mochizuki’s claimed proof, the 2021 PRIMS publication, and the unresolved disagreement described in the 2018 Scholze–Stix report and Mochizuki’s 2025 response.
Removed the diagram that falsely portrayed a simple exchange between three invented mathematical universes, and removed repeated self-links.
Restored the original publication date 2026-09-14 and removed the duplicate 2026-09-24 date.

meaning.note: Compared every localized section with the Japanese source: the conjecture statement and quantifiers, radical definition, IUT scope, publication-vs-proof distinction, the attributed Scholze–Stix criticism and Mochizuki response, and the conditional Fermat consequence.

terminology.note: Checked localized terminology for pairwise coprimality, radical, number field, Diophantine geometry, IUT, Hodge theaters, log-theta lattice, theorem/corollary, and conjecture status.

mathematics.note: Verified the standard ABC upper-bound form and its quantifiers. Corrected the earlier false inequality argument for Fermat: a hypothetical primitive solution yields infinitely many powered triples with fixed radical and unbounded c, contradicting ABC.
